design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing in one sentence: put the prepaid hours on the account. Nothing he says, and nothing on the face of the program record, says how many hours, at what price, or that anything stands between the request and the purchase. Both figures have to be built out of the ledger - the hours from eighteen months of drawing against blocks that expire, the price from a stepped rate, an itemised basis, a discount and an office release charge - and the second of them cannot be right until the agent has read, in the published pricing terms, that a block is priced only once the ceiling standing on the program carries a change dated in the current program year, seen on the program record that its last change was a change of address from before the term began, and carried out the review that is owed. An agent who prices the block against the stale published ceiling gets a number that is wrong by the whole office release charge and hears nothing about it from the caller.

SCOPE. Already occupied by task 0: the labor line for a completed call, the arrears late fee, the missed response credit and the account settlement figure, with their four tools. Claimed here: service_ext_credit_ceiling_review (the reviewed open balance ceiling written on the program) and service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price (the price of a block of prepaid hours), with the tools set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3 and purchase_hour_block_a465dc68. The two scopes are disjoint in policy, in tool and in subject: task 0 writes charge lines, a credit entry and a payment entry; this task amends one term of the program and books a block purchase. Nothing is reserved for later, since M is 2 and this is the last task; the difficulty's six policies are exactly the union of the two scopes.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, as printed by scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/service_dispatch_desk --tasks 2:
  {"task": 1, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/service_dispatch_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}
So one prerequisite problem, two computations, six factors each. The ceiling review takes six and the block price takes six.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price, the price of the block, which is what the caller asks for. One prerequisite problem, in a chain of two.
  Edge, root <- service_ext_credit_ceiling_review, kind value_input, gate ceiling_headroom, form state. Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the root policy's own rule: "A block of prepaid hours is priced only once the credit ceiling standing on the rate program carries a change dated in the current program year." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only once"; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state - the credit ceiling standing on the program and the date of the change it carries, both fields the program lookup returns; (3) it names no tool, no policy id and no code token; (4) its strength is a hard requirement with the scope the condition states, the current program year and no wider. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3 is the only action that writes a ceiling onto a program and stamps the change, so the derivation runs - the price waits on a ceiling changed in the current program year; the program record shows its last change to be a change of primary service address dated 2025-06-18, five months before the term began on 2025-12-01; the ceiling review policy's own rule says the ceiling it works out replaces the ceiling the program carried; therefore the review must be carried out first. Resolving action owner: agent. Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.service_programs.<program>.last_change_type = primary_site_changed, .last_change_date = 2025-06-18, .term_start_date = 2025-12-01, .credit_limit_usd = 75000.00, which is the tier's published figure carried over unreviewed. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the review leaves the block price at 54030.24 instead of 54181.02, because the headroom is measured against 75000.00 rather than 54300.00 and the office release charge falls away entirely.
  Topological order: the ceiling review, then the block purchase. There are no parallel edges to reorder: a chain of two has one order, and reversing it is not a second solution but a wrong one.
  No user hint: user_scenario never names the ceiling, the review, the headroom or the release charge, and never suggests anything must be settled first; the caller's only volunteered facts are that the hours have run dry, that the purchase order went across yesterday and that he will run the purchase himself. The tool layer validates nothing: purchase_hour_block_a465dc68 mints a row id from its three arguments and creates the purchase entry, reading the program row only for the customer reference, and never looks at the ceiling or at when it was last changed.

FACTOR CARD - service_ext_credit_ceiling_review (6 factors, base refs service_quote_and_approval, which owns the amendment of a live program term, with service_suspension_and_reinstatement and service_dispatch_and_response as the input lineage that reads the credit limit; trigger state_due; no override, since base fixes no basis for what a reviewed ceiling should be).
  review_window, method: from a restoration of privileges / from the term start / the last twelve months. Tier taken: the second, because the term began 2025-12-01 and has run nine of its twenty-four months and no reinstatement date stands, giving a ten-month window. Baseline reading: the last twelve months, giving 65920.00.
  starting_ceiling, method: the invoiced total rounded up to the next whole thousand where it stands between half the published credit limit and the whole of it / half the published credit limit where it stands at or below half / the published credit limit. Tier taken: the first, 39800.00 rounded to 40000.00 against a published limit of 75000.00. Baseline reading: the published credit limit, giving 95250.00.
  payment_record, parameter, multi-source: the strong record step at eight or more payments in the window with the most recent invoice to fall due no longer past its due day than the suspension period / the sound record step at four or more / no step. Tier taken: the first, 0.15, on eight payments and a most recent invoice twelve days past due against a thirty-day suspension period; every earlier invoice is paid in full. Baseline reading: no step, giving 48300.00.
  arrears_position, parameter, multi-source: the severe cut where the most recent invoice to fall due has stood past the suspension period and the window's unpaid balance passes the published limit / the mild cut where it stands past its due day, two or more fell due in the window and the payments do not clear them / nothing. Tier taken: the second, 0.10. Baseline reading: nothing cut, giving 58300.00.
  portfolio_position, parameter, cross-difficulty on maintenance, multi-source: the major step where an active agreement's annual price is at or above 20000 and its installments are cleared / the minor step where an active agreement's installments are cleared / no step. Tier taken: the first, 0.12, on the Labor Coverage Agreement at 38400.00 a year with four quarterly installments of 9600.00 matched by 38400.00 of payments. Baseline reading: no step, giving 49500.00.
  call_volume_allowance, parameter: the high volume allowance at twelve or more calls dispatched with two or more emergency dispatches / the standard allowance at six or more calls / nothing. Tier taken: the second, 7500.00, on seven calls dispatched in the window. Near-miss: the call accepted 2025-11-13 falls six days outside the ten-month window, whose earliest counted day is 2025-11-19, and a reader who counts it still lands on the same tier but on a different count; the emergency dispatch of 2025-06-26 falls outside it too. Baseline reading: no allowance, giving 46800.00.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 75000.00, the tier's published credit limit unchanged - which is exactly the figure an agent gets who reads the computation document and writes the program's existing ceiling straight back.

FACTOR CARD - service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price (6 factors, base ref service_block_hour_drawdown; trigger on_request; one declared override, of base's sentence that hours are bought in multiples of the tier's minimum purchase at the tier's block rate, replaced by the sentence that sizes the block to the shortfall).
  block_size_sold, method: as many whole multiples as cover the shortfall / no multiple where there is no shortfall / one multiple. Tier taken: the first, eight multiples of sixty hours, that is 480.0 hours, on a shortfall of 470.0. Baseline reading: one multiple, giving 7128.00.
  drawing_record_window, method: the tier's block expiry period where the tier rolls hours over and the term has not run out / from the term start where it does not / the last twelve months. Tier taken: the first, eighteen months. The block bought 2024-12-10 is twenty-one months old and its sixty hours have expired, but counting them changes nothing here, since 240.0 hours bought against 470.0 drawn still leaves nothing prepaid; the load-bearing near-miss of this computation is the labor invoice due 2025-08-28, exactly twelve months back, which if counted takes the ledger window's invoiced total to 67600.00 against 62850.00 paid and removes the good payer discount. Baseline reading: the last twelve months, giving 40629.60.
  stepped_block_rate, parameter, cross-difficulty on maintenance, multi-source: the block hour rate at the bulk share where two or more multiples are sold and an active agreement stands / at the volume share where two or more are sold and none stands / the block hour rate. Tier taken: the first, 120.00 at 0.94, that is 112.80. Baseline reading: the tier's block hour rate, giving 57265.50.
  price_basis, method: multiple by multiple, the first at the tier's rate and the rest at the stepped rate, where four or more are sold and unexpired blocks stand / the whole block at the stepped rate where two or three are sold / the whole block at the tier's rate. Tier taken: the first. Baseline reading: the whole block at the tier's rate, giving 57265.50.
  office_release_rate, parameter, multi-source: the strict rate where the price carries the open position past the ceiling and the most recent invoice to fall due stands past its due day / the standard rate where it carries it past the ceiling and that invoice does not / no charge. Tier taken: the first, 3.0 percent on an excess of 5026.00. Baseline reading: no release charge, giving 54030.24.
  settlement_record_discount, parameter, multi-source: the clear account discount where the window's payments cover what it invoiced and no open position stands / the good payer discount where they cover it and one does / no discount. Tier taken: the second, 1.0 percent. Baseline reading: no discount, giving 54726.78.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 7200.00, one sixty-hour multiple at the published rate, against gold 54181.02.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Two subjects, and the governing lineage taken per subject.
  service_program_updated (the ceiling review): governed by service_quote_and_approval alone, whose two eligibility gates, the recorded owner approval and the no-reissue-after-approval rule, both apply to the issuing of a written quote and not to an amendment of a program term; neither is skipped, because neither applies. It is inherited as policy scope: what the ceiling review writes is a term of the live program, amended one term at a time and dated, exactly as that policy provides for the credit limit, the purchase order requirement and the primary site.
  service_block_hours_purchased (the block purchase): governed by service_block_hour_drawdown, whose eligibility block_purchase_order_on_file does apply. Authority: system record. Evidence: the intake lodged 2026-09-17, request_type block_purchase_order, outcome approved, carrying the program reference. Correlation: service_requests.program_id bound to the action's program_id argument, which is the same program the hours are credited to. Timing: pre-action, the order having reached the office the day before the call. The rest of that policy is inherited and honoured rather than overridden: hours are bought in multiples of the tier's minimum purchase, they are drawn down oldest block first, they expire at the tier's expiry period counted forward in whole calendar months, and unused hours roll over at this tier - all four are read by the computation. What the declared override replaces is the single sentence that a block is simply bought at the tier's block rate, since the price here is sized and stepped.
  There is no time eligibility on either subject, so temporal_feasibility is empty. The tier's own clocks are still honoured in the computation: the eighteen-month expiry period is counted forward in whole calendar months from each purchase day, and the review window is counted in whole and part months from the term start.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The ceiling review's object is the one rate program on the account, correlated by the program reference; it amends that program's ceiling and nothing else, and the rows entering its aggregates are the charge lines with a due day inside the ten-month window (seven of them, 39800.00) and the payments received inside it (eight, 35050.00). Excluded by a visible key: the labor invoice due 2025-08-28 and the parts invoice due 2025-10-20, both outside the window, together with the payments of 2025-10-05 and 2025-11-02 that cleared them. The block purchase's object is the same program, and the rows entering its aggregates are the three blocks bought inside the tier's eighteen-month expiry period and the ten calls completed inside it. Excluded: the block bought 2024-12-10, expired. The written purchase order is correlated to the program by its program reference, and no second order stands lodged on the account.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The customer, two sites and three units: the account, the data centre whose CRAC unit drives the call volume, and the medical pavilion the maintenance agreement runs at. The rate program: the tier every published figure comes from, its term start fixing the review window, and its stale ceiling and stale cached balances - block_hours_remaining of 24.0 against a real position of nothing, emergency_calls_remaining of 9 against three dispatches counted out of twelve, and while balance_due of 4750.00 is exactly the ledger's open position - and no rule reads the two hour and dispatch figures. The four blocks: three unexpired inside the eighteen-month period and one from 2024-12-10 that has expired, which is the near-miss on the prepaid position. The ten completed calls: 470.0 hours drawn inside eighteen months of which 355.0 fall inside twelve, so the window factor genuinely moves the size of the block; remove the call of 2025-06-27 and both the shortfall and the multiples change. The eleven dispatch rows: the call count the volume allowance rests on, two of them still open with no completion row, which is why the count of calls dispatched and the hours drawn do not move together. The three emergency dispatches: the second half of the high volume condition, which is not met. The nine charge lines and ten payments: the invoiced total and the payments of the review window, the count of each, the days past due of the most recent invoice, which is the only invoice standing unpaid, and the open position of 4750.00 that the headroom is measured from; the pair from outside the window (the 22000.00 labor invoice due 2025-08-28 and the 5800.00 parts invoice due 2025-10-20, with the payments that cleared them) is what makes the twelve-month ledger window and the ten-month review window give different answers, which is what the review_window factor turns on. The written purchase order: the intake the block purchase gate requires, lodged the day before the call. The maintenance agreement and its eight installment and payment rows: the cross-difficulty evidence for the portfolio step and for the stepped block rate. The expired filtration programme: a second contract at the medical pavilion that a careful agent rules out on its standing, and the parent row the demand ledger's program reference resolves to under the scenario's shared register numbering. Base automatic clauses were checked against this seed: no invoice has stood past the tier's thirty-day suspension period, so nothing is suspendable; the renewal window does not open, since the term ends 2027-11-30; no block expires between frozen_time and the writes; the emergency allowance was credited once at activation and three of the twelve dispatches are used, so no surcharge is owed.

PERSONA. Marcus Oyelaran is brisk, mid-task and slightly impatient, and the voice is different from the first task's caller: shorter sentences, an engineering lead waiting behind him, and a flat refusal to guess at figures he regards as the desk's own record. He volunteers the surface goal (the hours have run dry; the purchase order went across yesterday; put the hours on the account now), the authorisation boundary (the desk may do what it must on its side; the purchase is his to run), and nothing else. Given only when asked: the account number 620398 and the tax digits 2247, the building names, the unit tag CRAC-2, the maintenance agreement at the pavilion and the purchase order requirement. Explicit cannot-answer branches: the internal customer reference, which he has never had; the prepaid hour balance, which he refers to the portal with the observation that it has shown the same figure for weeks, an honest reading of a cache the seed really does leave stale; and what the account owes, which he will not put a figure on. Reacted to only after the agent speaks: agreement that the desk should do what it needs to, acceptance of the priced figure without questioning its make-up, running the purchase once it is handed over, and closing when a purchase reference comes back. He never mentions the credit ceiling or its review, and he never corrects a wrong price.

THE DEPENDENCY, LONG AND BROAD. Long: the goal names a purchase; the pricing terms make the price wait on a record-visible state of the program; that state is brought about by a second computation which is itself a six-factor reconciliation of the account's whole record. Two hops, and they cannot be swapped, because the headroom the price is measured against is the ceiling the review writes. Broad: the review reads the invoice and payment ledger over a window it first has to work out, the count of payments and of invoices, the days past due, the call and emergency dispatch counts, and the other account's price and installment ledger; the price reads the block purchase ledger over the tier's expiry period, the completed-call hours over a window it also has to work out, the whole invoice and payment ledger for the open position, the days past due again and the maintenance agreement's existence. Remove any one of them and a figure moves, as the factor sensitivity runs show.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG. Pricing the block before the ceiling is reviewed, and losing the whole office release charge. Reading the record over twelve months rather than from the term start, which moves the starting ceiling from 40000.00 to 46000.00 and the ceiling to 65920.00. Counting the expired 2024-12-10 block into the prepaid position and selling one multiple fewer. Reading the drawing record over twelve months rather than the tier's eighteen, and selling six multiples instead of eight. Applying the stepped rate to the whole block rather than to the multiples beyond the first. Taking the discount off after the release charge instead of off the block price alone. Applying the three ceiling steps one after another instead of combining them into one factor. Rounding the starting ceiling down rather than up to the next whole thousand.

THE STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the account by the company name; verify on the account number and the tax digits. Read the program, the sites, the equipment, the whole service history, the lodged requests, the maintenance agreement and its ledger, and the air quality programs. See in the pricing terms that the block is priced only once the ceiling carries a change dated in the current program year, and on the program that its last change was a change of address dated before the term began. Work the review: ten-month window, 39800.00 invoiced, starting ceiling 40000.00, plus 0.15 and 0.12 less 0.10 combined into one factor, plus the 7500.00 volume allowance, giving 54300.00, and write it. Then work the price: eighteen-month drawing window, 470.0 hours drawn against 180.0 unexpired, a shortfall of 470.0 needing eight sixty-hour multiples, 480.0 hours; the first multiple at 120.00 and the further seven at 112.80, that is 54576.00; less the 1.0 percent good payer discount of 545.76; plus 3.0 percent on the 5026.00 by which the price passes the 49550.00 headroom, that is 150.78; giving 54181.02. Unlock the purchase and hand it to the caller, who runs it.

CLOSURE. service_ext_credit_ceiling_review -> set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3 -> step 11, credit_limit_usd -> 54300.00 -> the program carries a ceiling of 54300.00 and a credit ceiling change dated 2026-09-18. service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price -> purchase_hour_block_a465dc68 -> step 13, purchase_amount_usd -> 54181.02 -> a block purchase entry crediting 480.0 hours at 54181.02, bought by the owner himself. The write order 11, 13 is the topological order of the chain; charter_scope.extended_policies equals the computation policy ids and the whole tree; required_documents repeats it in order; charter_scope.task_tools equals the two tools in first-use order; no handoff is called and nothing hangs outside the tree.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD, AND THE DRAFT RECOMPUTATION. The review inherits its one governing policy as policy scope and cites the program's own stale ceiling and last-change stamp as the pre-action obligation, since it is state_due and no caller intent selects it; the purchase is on_request, its intent is the caller's own verbatim line, its discriminator phrase occurs in that line, and its one real gate is the written purchase order lodged the day before, bound through service_requests.program_id to the program the hours are credited to. Draft recomputation with the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this rationale masked: from the published pricing terms, the tool schemas, what the share tools return and what the caller says, a reader sees that the price waits on a ceiling changed in the current program year, finds the program's last change to be an address change from before the term, carries out the review on the ledger, then sizes and prices the block and hands the purchase to the caller because the terms reserve it to the owner and he says he will run it. The draft agrees with gold on both figures, on the 480.0 hours, on the order and on the hand-over, and no second reading of the published prose gives another.

user_scenario:
Marcus Oyelaran is the asset manager for Verity Health Realty LLC, which owns a colocation data centre off Halsted and a medical pavilion out in Evergreen Park, and he is the one who lives with the mechanical bills for both. He calls late in the afternoon, plainly mid-task, because the block of prepaid technician hours on the demand service account has run dry again and his engineering lead has two jobs queued behind it. He puts it simply: the purchase order for more hours went across to the office yesterday afternoon, and he wants the desk to put the prepaid hours on the account now, priced and credited, so the queued work can be dispatched against them rather than billed at the walk-up rate. He is content for the desk to do whatever it has to do on its own side of the account to get that done, and says so if he is told there is something to settle first; the purchase itself, though, is his to make, and he says he would rather run it himself than have someone put a number through on his behalf, so he will take it on when it is handed to him.

He gives his name and the company without prompting. If he is asked to prove who he is he reads the account number 620398 off the last invoice and, if one detail will not do, the last four of the tax number, 2247. Ask him for whatever internal reference the office files him under and he will say he has never had one and would not know where to look.

Asked, he can say that the data centre is the Halsted Exchange building and the unit that keeps pulling technicians out there is CRAC-2, that the medical pavilion carries a maintenance agreement of its own which he keeps quite separate in his head, and that the office insists on a purchase order number on every invoice. He does not know how many prepaid hours are left, saying only that the portal has been showing the same figure for weeks and he stopped believing it; he does not know what the account owes either, and will not put a figure on it when pressed, because he says that is the desk's own record and not his.

If the agent tells him the hours have been priced, or that anything has been changed or written on the account, he takes it as read and does not question it, and he does not ask what the figure is made up of. Once the purchase is handed over for him to run himself, he puts it through and says only that it is done. When a purchase reference comes back he says that is all he needed, thanks the agent for turning it round and rings off. Until the hours are priced or the purchase is handed to him he waits: he does not push, he does not ask what else the desk might need to do, and he offers nothing about the account that he has not been asked for.

gold_actions.business_effect: The open balance ceiling standing on the rate program is replaced by the reviewed figure of 54300.00 and the program is stamped as having had its credit ceiling changed on 2026-09-18, so the account's headroom is measured against the ceiling its own record carries.

base_preconditions.condition: service_quote_and_approval governs the terms of a live rate program and their amendment: the thresholds above which work is quoted, approved and carries a deposit, the validity of a quote and the deposit portion. evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the account of the building owner calling, by the company name he states, and read back the account number, the tax identification digits, the agreed credit terms and the account standing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the account can be read or written until the account is identified; it supplies the customer reference every later lookup and both writes are keyed to.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Check the account number and the tax identification digits the caller states against the profile on file and record the verification for this call.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The desk changes no term and books no purchase on an account until the caller has passed verification on this call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the demand service rate program: the tier held, its standing, the term dates, the prepaid hour balance shown, the open balance ceiling standing on it and the kind and date of the last change made to its terms.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier fixes the published block rate, the minimum purchase, the expiry period and the published credit limit; the term start fixes the review window; and the kind and date of the last term change is what shows whether the ceiling standing on the program has been set since the term began.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the buildings on the account with their use class and dispatch region.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The calls whose hours are being reconciled are spread over both buildings, and the maintenance agreement runs at one of them, which the block rate ladder turns on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the equipment register so the units the recent calls were worked on can be placed at their buildings.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It confirms that the hours drawn belong to this account's own equipment and that the unit the caller names is on the register.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole demand service history of the rate program: blocks of prepaid hours bought with their purchase and expiry dates, calls dispatched and completed with their hours, emergency dispatches counted, invoices with their due days and every payment received.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every aggregate of both computations comes from these rows: the invoiced total and the payments in the review window, the count of payments and of invoices, the calls dispatched and emergency dispatches counted, the hours drawn over the drawing window, the unexpired block hours and the open position.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Look up what the owner has lodged on the demand service side, with what each names and how far it has been carried.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The written purchase order for the block stands on file as an approved intake, which is what the terms require to be on file before prepaid hours are bought.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the preventive maintenance agreement the owner also holds: the tier, whether it stands active, the building it runs at and its annual price.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Whether an active agreement stands, and what its annual price is, decides both the rate the block steps to and the portfolio step in the ceiling review.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the maintenance agreement's own ledger: the installments that fell due in the last twelve months and the payments received against them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Whether that account's installments are cleared is the second half of the portfolio step's condition in the ceiling review.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the air quality and filtration programs on the account, with their standing and term dates.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The filtration programme at the medical pavilion ran out at its 2024 term end and stands expired, so no other contract on the account bears on the prepaid hours or on the ceiling being reviewed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the action that writes a reviewed open balance ceiling onto the rate program.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes no record.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Write the reviewed open balance ceiling onto the rate program, so the account's headroom is measured against the ceiling its current record carries.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reviewed ceiling is the figure service_ext_credit_ceiling_review computes; scoring unwraps to the underlying task tool.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.program_id: Value: 1730d7a0-691c-4a2b-8db2-068b1f4d6e65. Basis: the tool's own schema states of this parameter, "Id class - the reference number of the demand service rate program", and the company's terms on holding more than one program state, "An account carries one demand service rate program at a time." Uniqueness: the rate program lookup at action 2, keyed on the customer reference the account lookup returned, comes back with exactly one program row, the Critical Facility Response Program standing active on term 2025-12-01 to 2027-11-30; there is no second program to confuse it with, and the reference is read from that row rather than stated by the caller.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_limit_usd: Value: 54300.00. The term began 2025-12-01 and has run nine whole months against the tier's twenty-four, and no reinstatement stands on the program, so the record is read from the term start, ten months. Inside that window 39800.00 fell due on seven invoices and 35050.00 was received across eight payments. 39800.00 is above half the tier's published credit limit of 75000.00 and not above it, so the starting ceiling is 39800.00 rounded up to the next whole thousand, 40000.00. Eight payments inside the window and a most recent invoice to fall due only twelve days past its due day, no longer than the tier's thirty-day suspension period, give the strong record step of 0.15. That invoice standing past its due day, seven invoices fallen due in the window and payments that do not clear what was invoiced give the mild arrears cut of 0.10. The owner's active Labor Coverage Agreement at 38400.00 a year, with its four installments of 9600.00 cleared, gives the major portfolio step of 0.12. Seven calls dispatched in the window, below twelve but at or above six, give the standard volume allowance of 7500.00. 40000.00 x (1 + 0.15 + 0.12 - 0.10) = 46800.00, plus 7500.00, is 54300.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the block purchase and hand it to the caller, who is buying the hours himself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Buying prepaid hours is the owner's own act; the agent unlocks it and the caller runs it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Buy the block of prepaid technician hours the account's drawing record calls for, at the price the terms give, so the hours are credited to the program and the queued work can be drawn against them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The price of the block is what service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price computes; scoring unwraps to the underlying task tool.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.program_id: Value: 1730d7a0-691c-4a2b-8db2-068b1f4d6e65. Basis: the tool's own schema states of this parameter, "Id class - the reference number of the demand service rate program the hours are credited to", and the company's terms on holding more than one program state, "An account carries one demand service rate program at a time." Uniqueness: the rate program lookup at action 2, keyed on the customer reference the account lookup returned, comes back with exactly one program row, the Critical Facility Response Program standing active on term 2025-12-01 to 2027-11-30; there is no second program to confuse it with, and the reference is read from that row rather than stated by the caller.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.block_hours: Value: 480.0. Basis: the published pricing terms state, "A block of prepaid hours is sold as a single one of the tier's minimum purchase multiples" and "Where the shortfall stands above one of the tier's minimum purchase multiples, as many whole multiples are sold as it takes to cover the shortfall, rounded up", with "The hours sold are the multiples sold multiplied by the tier's minimum purchase." Uniqueness: the tier lets unused hours roll over and the term has run nine of its twenty-four months, so the drawing record is read over the tier's eighteen-month expiry period; the completed calls inside it total 470.0 hours against 180.0 hours of unexpired blocks, leaving nothing prepaid and a shortfall of 470.0 hours, which needs eight whole sixty-hour multiples. Eight multiples of sixty is 480.0 hours, stated in decimal hours to one decimal place as the schema requires.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.purchase_amount_usd: Value: 54181.02. Eight multiples are sold, at or above the stepped multiple count of two, and an active preventive maintenance agreement stands on the account, so the rate the block steps to is the tier's block hour rate of 120.00 at the bulk share of 0.94, that is 112.80; because eight multiples are at or above the bulk multiple count of four and unexpired blocks already stand on the program, the block is priced multiple by multiple, the first sixty hours at 120.00 and the further seven multiples at 112.80: 7200.00 + 47376.00 = 54576.00. Payments of 62850.00 inside the twelve-month ledger window cover the 45600.00 invoiced in it while an open position stands, so the good payer discount of 1.0 percent comes off the block price, 545.76. The open position is everything invoiced on the program over its life, 67600.00, less every payment received, 62850.00, that is 4750.00; the headroom is the 54300.00 ceiling now standing on the program less that, 49550.00; the block price passes it by 5026.00 and the most recent invoice to fall due stands past its due day, so the office release charge runs at 3.0 percent on the excess, 150.78. 54576.00 - 545.76 + 150.78 = 54181.02.

edges.condition: The rate program's most recent term change is a change of the credit ceiling and its date falls in the current program year.
edges.policy_source: A block of prepaid hours is priced only once the credit ceiling standing on the rate program carries a change dated in the current program year.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The most recent change to the program's terms is recorded as a change of primary service address, not of the credit ceiling, and it is dated 2025-06-18, five months before the current term started on 2025-12-01. The ceiling of 75000.00 standing on the program is therefore the tier's published figure carried over unreviewed, and no change of the credit ceiling stands dated since the term began.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The ceiling review writes 54300.00 onto the program and stamps the change as a credit ceiling change dated 2026-09-18, so the headroom the release charge is measured against falls from 70250.00 to 49550.00 and the block price rises from 54030.24 to 54181.02.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain of two problems with one edge, so there is no pair of writes free to be reordered: the ceiling review must land before the purchase is priced, and the purchase is the root. Reversing them is not a second solution but a wrong one, because the price would be measured against the ceiling the program carried from before the term began.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the ceiling review and replaying everything else leaves the block price at 54030.24 instead of 54181.02: the headroom stays at the 75000.00 published ceiling less the open position, the block price no longer carries the account past it, and the office release charge falls from 150.78 to nothing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks only for the prepaid hours to be put on the account and priced, and says he sent the purchase order across yesterday. He never mentions the credit ceiling, the review the terms owe it, the headroom or the office release charge, and he never suggests that anything must be settled first; the one thing he will say if the agent raises it is that he does not know how many hours are left and has stopped believing the portal. The existence of the prerequisite reaches the agent only through the sentence in the published pricing terms that a block is priced only once the ceiling standing on the program carries a change dated in the current program year, and through the program record showing its last change to be a change of primary service address dated before the term began.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: purchase_hour_block_a465dc68 mints a row id from its three arguments and creates the block purchase entry, reading the program row only to carry the customer reference onto the entry; it never looks at the credit ceiling, the last change type or the last change date, so it books whatever hours and price it is given while the ceiling still stands unreviewed. It raises no error and gives no hint, and set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3 likewise writes whatever ceiling it is given without testing anything about the account.
